newsitem.title: USA: Billion-dollar suit against Lucent Tech settled.
newsitem.headline: Billion-dollar suit against Lucent Tech settled.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp and DSC Communications Corp have settled a $1.6 billion suit against Lucent Technologies Inc, the clerk's office of the U.S. District Court confirmed Thursday.
Details of the settlement were not included in court papers, only a stipulation of dismissal signed by all parties, a spokeswoman for the clerk's office said.
Bell Atlantic spokesman Eric Rabe told Reuters the details of the settlement will not be released.
"But we're very pleased with this," he said.
"We do an awful lot of business with Lucent -- hundreds of millions of dollars a year. All parties have acted in good faith and are mending the relationships."
Officials of Lucent and DSC could not be reached for comment.
Bell Atlantic had sought $900 million and DSC $725.4 in the suit accusing Lucent of controlling the telephone equipment market.
Lucent allegedly delayed technology and software DSC claimed was needed to proceed with the product it was trying to market.

A second defendent in the case, AT&T Corp, settled with Bell Atlantic and DSC on February 18. The terms were not disclosed. The plaintiffs charged AT&T with crippling Caller ID by blocking that information on most long-distance calls.
Lucent Technologies spun off from AT&T as a separate company in February 1996, shortly before the suit was filed.
